items.note: Duplicated nb:nb26-calc-032 (hypokalemia 2.8 mEq/L -> expect flat T waves/U waves). Rewritten as a recognize-cues item on the findings of hypernatremia from water deficit.

Duplicated fluids-main-q5 and fluids-main-q1 (hyperkalemia with peaked T waves: calcium, insulin with dextrose, albuterol). Rewritten as a SATA on safe IV calcium gluconate administration; difficulty set to 2/Apply to match.

Magnesium of 4.8 mg/dL is too low to explain absent reflexes and a respiratory rate of 9/min (reflexes are typically lost around 7-10 mg/dL and respiratory depression occurs at higher levels). Changed the level to 10.4 mg/dL so the key is consistent.

Duplicated fluids-main-q2 and nclex-highrisk-q3 (increased ICP: question a hypotonic/D5W fluid). Rewritten as an analyze-cues item on questioning IV saline in hypervolemic (dilutional) hyponatremia from heart failure.

Label: the item tests correct daily-weight technique (hydration monitoring, a Basic Care and Comfort task), not Reduction of Risk Potential. Relabeled rrp -> bcc (counts stay within target: rrp 11/12, bcc 5/4).
Duplicated rnr:integ-027 (day 3 after 40% burns, diuresis and crackles: fluid remobilization and overload). Rewritten as a prioritize-hypotheses item on postoperative third spacing.

Duplicated nb:nb26-gios-035 (adult burns on LR titrated to urine output: which hourly output is adequate; same 0.5 mL/kg/hr fact). Rewritten as an evaluate-outcomes item on response to fluid replacement after vomiting.

Duplicated nb:nb26-core-001 (older adult with orthostatic dizziness asking to walk to the bathroom: dangle, then assist). Rewritten as a safety item on preventing pathologic fractures and falls in hypercalcemia from multiple myeloma; clientNeed kept safety.
